description: Direct check of C-append-log-identity-consistency: drive a follower whose stored suffix conflicts with an incoming leader term, make the subsequent StoreLogs fail once after DeleteRange has succeeded, then send an otherwise valid AppendEntries starting at the truncated index. The oracle is the follower's own acceptance of that subsequent request (accepted == true); identity is the single node the whole history belongs to. A rejected probe after a successful replication to the surviving prefix is the violating observation, because the stated responsibility is that the cached last log identity must not make the node reject every subsequent AppendEntries for the removed range.

harness.description: In-package Go test that seeds a log suffix, injects a LogStore whose StoreLogs fails once, drives appendEntries through the real handler, and observes the follower's cached last log identity and its acceptance of a later request. Uses only real target code and a faithfully failing LogStore; no protocol logic is altered.
semantic_changes: skipStartup is set so the main goroutine does not run; appendEntries is invoked directly with a real RPC struct, so the handler logic under test is unchanged.
The LogStore wrapper fails exactly one StoreLogs call to expose the error path; all other store behaviour is the in-repository InmemStore.

legality.derivation: appendEntries is the follower entry point for replicated entries; the LogStore interface contract allows StoreLogs and DeleteRange to fail independently, so a log store that fails StoreLogs after DeleteRange succeeded is a legal caller-supplied object. Calling the handler directly with a real RPC struct exercises the same code that the rpcCh path would invoke.
legality.applicability: The node is a Follower with a stored suffix and no leaders; the injected LogStore is faithful except for the single simulated failure. The proposition is local to this node and does not assume a cluster consequence.
unresolved: Whether a production LogStore fails StoreLogs after DeleteRange succeeded.
alternatives: A later successful store or a restart repairs the cached identity.

grounding.derivation: After the truncated range is re-sent from the surviving prefix, the stored prefix still matches the incoming PrevLog, so a node whose reported last log identity is consistent with its store accepts the entries and stores them; rejection is attributable to the stale cached index driving r.logs.GetLog on a removed index.
grounding.applicability: The probe is admitted only for the node that experienced the conflict and StoreLogs failure, correlated by node and the truncated index recorded on the prerequisite events.
alternatives: The rejection could also be attributed to an unrelated Term or PrevLog mismatch, which the harness holds fixed at the same leader term and surviving prefix.

observable_properties.description: A follower that has truncated a conflicting suffix and then failed its store call must still accept an otherwise valid AppendEntries that restarts at the truncated index once its store is healthy; the compared field is the handler's own Success result.

uncertainties: The check exercises a single follower with an artificial single-shot store failure; it does not establish how often a production store fails this way.
